report.notes: Agent review as instructed by the guide. Reviewer verified its central finding by executing the real code rather than reasoning about it, and I reproduced it independently before fixing: a runner throwing Object.create(null) made run() reject with 'Cannot convert object to primitive value', leaving 1 job abandoned in the queue. Both in-scope findings are now fixed; npm test 12/12 (was 10, +2 new tests), tsc clean for changed code, and the reproduction probe now returns {ran:1,failed:1} with the following job having run.

findings.description: src/jobs/JobQueue.ts: `error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)` is evaluated inside run()'s catch, and String(err) can itself throw. Verified by executing the code: a runner that throws Object.create(null) raises TypeError 'Cannot convert object to primitive value', and one that throws an object with a throwing toString raises that error; in both cases run() rejects, the {ran, failed} tally is lost, and every job queued behind the failing one is abandoned. This falsifies the exact invariant the change leaned on: the new enqueue guard's docstring justifies itself with 'a throw inside run() would abandon every job still queued behind it', and run()'s docstring promises 'A failing job is logged and dropped; the rest still run'. The empty-request-id hole was hardened while the sibling hole in the same catch block was left open.
findings.dispositionReason: Extracted a describeError(unknown) helper that wraps the stringification in its own try/catch and falls back to '<thrown value could not be described>'. It also coerces err.message via String(), so an Error subclass with a non-string or throwing message getter is contained by the same guard. Reproduced the failure first (run() rejected, 1 job abandoned), then confirmed the fix: the same probe now returns {ran:1,failed:1} with the following job run.

findings.description: The tests covered only `throw new Error(...)`. The String(err) branch, added deliberately because a job may throw a non-Error, had no test at all, which is precisely why the crash above went unnoticed.
findings.dispositionReason: Added two tests. One covers the ordinary non-Error branch (a thrown string and a thrown plain object, asserting {ran:0,failed:2} and the logged error text). The other is the regression test for the defect above: it throws Object.create(null) and an object with a throwing toString, then asserts the queue still returns {ran:1,failed:2}, drains to size 0, and logs both failures under their own request ids. That second test fails against the pre-fix code.

findings.description: The failure line flattens the thrown value to a single string under the neutral key `error`, so only AppLogger's value/text redaction applies (SECRET_VALUE and SECRET_IN_TEXT at src/platform/logging/AppLogger.ts:19-20); the key-based rule (SECRET_KEY, line 18) can never fire on it. Verified by execution: an error message containing {"token":"hunter2secret","api_key":"sk_live_abcdefgh"} is logged verbatim, because neither the JSON-key shape nor the sk_live_ prefix matches the two text patterns. The Bearer and sk- shapes the new test exercises are redacted correctly. This is a limitation of the pre-existing redaction engine rather than new redaction code, and relying on that engine is what r-eftp2zdb6as643np asks for -- but this change is the first path that funnels arbitrary third-party error text into a log line, so the pre-existing gap now has a much wider mouth, which bears on RULES.md #1.
findings.dispositionReason: valid-deferred: the fix belongs in AppLogger's redaction patterns, not in this ticket. Widening those patterns changes redaction behaviour for every existing caller and deserves its own ticket with its own review, rather than riding along on a job-traceability change.

report.notes: Round-1 review fixes were applied before that round was reported, so this IMPLEMENT pass had no remaining work; no further edits were made. State of the fix: src/jobs/JobQueue.ts now routes the thrown value through a describeError(unknown) helper that contains its own stringification failure, replacing the inline `err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)` that could throw out of run()'s catch. src/jobs/JobQueue.test.ts gained two tests -- ordinary non-Error throws (string, plain object), and the regression test that throws Object.create(null) and an object with a throwing toString, asserting the queue still returns {ran:1,failed:2} and drains. npm test 12/12 pass; tsc --noEmit reports no errors in changed code; the standalone reproduction probe that previously showed run() rejecting with 1 job abandoned now returns {ran:1,failed:1} with the following job run. findings.description: The round-1 fix contained the ARGUMENT (describeError) but not the CALL. log.error("job failed", {...}) sits inside run()'s catch, and AppLogger#emit invokes the sink synchronously, so a throwing sink escapes the catch and rejects run(), abandoning every job still queued. This throw site is new: pre-fix the catch was literally `catch { failed++; }`, incapable of throwing. It violates the invariant the fix's own docstring states -- that an escaping throw there would make one job's failure become the whole queue's failure. The empty catch carries a comment explaining why nothing is done there: the logger is the only reporting channel, so a failure to log has nowhere to be reported, but it must not cost the queue. Added a test ('a sink that throws does not abandon the rest of the queue either') that constructs a JobQueue whose sink always throws, fails the first of two jobs, and asserts {ran:1,failed:1}, that the innocent job ran, and that the queue drained. # Handover: T-2 failed jobs are traceable (2026-09-20)

Targeted autonomous session, `/story auto T-2`. One item, done and committed as `122442a` on `main`.

## Completed

- **T-2: Make failed background jobs traceable to the originating request.** `JobQueue` takes an optional `Sink` (same shape `Router` already used) and, per job, builds an `AppLogger` bound to that job's own `requestId`. It logs one `error` line when the job throws, and hands the same logger to the runner. Tests: `src/jobs/JobQueue.test.ts` (7) and `src/http/handler.test.ts` (1, end-to-end). Suite is 13/13.

## Decisions

- **The runner gets the logger, not just the failure path.** r-p19bbvh0jhj8xgma says *anything* a running job logs is under the enqueuing request's id. Logging only the queue's own failure line satisfies half of that: a runner left to build its own logger can reach for `withRequestId(randomUUID(), ...)` just as easily as the correct call. So `JobRunner` widened to `(job, log) => ...`, mirroring how `Router` hands route handlers a pre-bound `log`. Backward compatible -- a one-parameter function stays assignable.
- **T-2 now cites r-p19bbvh0jhj8xgma and r-eftp2zdb6as643np.** It cited nothing when picked, though the 09-15 jobs ruling was made for exactly this work. Citation added at PLAN so the rulings reach anyone working the item.
- **Containment in `run()` is the hard part, not the logging.** Two review rounds, each catching a real way one job's failure became the whole queue's failure, both verified by executing the code rather than reading it:
  1. `String(err)` can itself throw -- `Object.create(null)`, a throwing `toString` -- and it ran inside `run()`'s catch. Now contained in a `describeError` helper.
  2. The fix contained the *argument* but not the *call*. `log.error` reaches the sink synchronously, so a throwing sink (destroyed stdout, buggy custom `Sink`) escaped the catch the same way. Now `failed++` happens before logging and the log call is itself wrapped.
  The generalisable lesson: pre-fix the catch was `catch { failed++; }`, incapable of throwing. Every statement added to a catch block that guards a loop invariant is a new way to break it, and the helper that formats the error counts.
- **`enqueue` refuses an empty or whitespace-only request id**, matching `AppLogger`'s own `trim()` guard, so an untraceable job never enters the queue and `run()` has no reason to throw. Breaks no caller: `Router.dispatch` builds its logger first, so the HTTP path fails earlier.

## Continuation

- **T-3 Move AppLogger into packages/logging** is the next ticket. Note it now has one more importer than it did: `src/jobs/JobQueue.ts` imports `AppLogger` and `Sink`, alongside `src/http/router.ts` and the two test files.
- **ISS-004 (redaction misses non-Bearer/sk- secret shapes)** is the one worth doing soon, and T-2 is why. `AppLogger`'s key-based rule only fires on a real object key, so a secret inside a flat string is caught only if it matches `sk-...` or `Bearer ...`. T-2 is the first path that funnels arbitrary third-party error text into a log line, so `ghp_`, `xoxb-`, `AKIA`, JWTs and `password=` in a URL now reach a line unredacted -- which is RULES.md #1. Deliberately not fixed here: widening those patterns changes redaction for every existing caller and wants its own review.

## Also filed

- **ISS-001** (medium): an empty `x-request-id` header is accepted as a request id -- `?? randomUUID()` does not substitute for `""` -- so `AppLogger.withRequestId("")` throws out of `app.handle()` and the request logs nothing at all.
- **ISS-003** (low): `tsconfig.json` declares `strict`/`noEmit` but nothing typechecks -- no `typecheck` script, no `@types/node`. A genuine type error in a new test this session was caught only because `tsc` happened to be installed globally. Adding types is a devDependency decision against RULES.md #2, so it needs an owner's call.
- **ISS-002**: duplicate of ISS-001, resolved. It was auto-filed by a `deferred` finding disposition after I had already filed ISS-001 by hand.

## Notes for the next session

- The codex review bridge reports healthy via `storybloq_health`, but neither `review_plan` nor `review_code` is callable from a Claude Code session here; both review stages fell back to agent review. Worth checking before assuming codex review is running.
- Unstaged and unrelated, left alone: `.continuity-mcp.json`, `.story/.gitignore`.
